newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end steady but gold still weak.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end steady but gold still weak.

text.p: New York precious metals futures ended steady Wednesday, on moderate volumes, but not before gold fell to new three-year lows.

"There wasn't a great deal of activity today, but the gold market still feels under some pressure, despite the decision by Eurostat (the EC statistics bureau) ruling out the use of central bank gold sales to improve fiscal deficits to meet EMU criteria," Chase Manhattan New York managing director, Dinsa Mehta said.
COMEX April gold ended unchanged at $346.40 an ounce, but not before posting new contract lows at $344.30.
In the bullion market, spot gold ended quoted $343.90/40, after fixing at $343.40 in London Wednesday afternoon, compared to the New York close Tuesday around $344.00/50.

Gold prices saw fresh three year lows last week, on more concern about central bank sales and a seasonal dip in demand during the Ramadan and Chinese New Year holidays, with a strong US dollar limiting investor interest in gold also.
But nervous producer hedging was also beginning to be seen, traders said.
"All in all, 1997 should be a very interesting year," Merrill Lynch analyst Ted Arnold said. "The bear market has clearly begun."

"We have already seen 1300 tonnes of gold sold by European central banks since the Maastricht Treaty was signed in 1992 and we would be very surprised if this year did not bring sales of at least another 300 to 500 tonnes."
In addition, "there are ten mines in South Africa at present with working costs of at least $350 an ounce and four with costs over $380," Arnold said.

"Some of these mines may decide to lock in their forward dollar gold prices and rand gold prices and if that happens we could see perhaps up to another 100 to 200 tonnes of forward sales on price rallies," he said.
Gold was again weaker than silver Wednesday, with the spot gold/silver ratio edging back down to 70.65, from 70.78 at Tuesday's close, after seeing a 15 month low at 69.79 last Friday.
COMEX March silver ended up 1.5 cents at $4.872 an ounce, after trading down to a intraday low at $4.810.
In the platinum metals group, NYMEX April platinum closed up $1.20 at $356.40, while NYMEX March palladium ended up five cents at $129.75, continuing its recovery of the past six weeks.

"The situation regarding Russian palladium shipments is that the Russian state PGM trading agency has not yet signed annual sales agreements with Japanese customers," CPM Group analyst Ted Kempf said.
"The Russian government has wanted to reduce its annual palladium exports since late 1995 at least but was unable to do so in 1996."
"It may do so in 1997 and CPM Group projects a sharp decline in Russian palladium shipments this year."
"The reduction has caused Japanese dealers to cover some of their needs elsewhere, which has led to some purchases in the dealer market and upward pressure on prices."
Russia accounts for about 54 percent of world palladium supply.
((-Clive McKeef, New York Commodities Desk, +1-212-859-1641 -email: clive.mckeef@reuters.com))
